signature.name: Hagia Sophia
signature.detail: The defining monument of Istanbul, a vast former cathedral turned mosque whose dome and mosaics have awed visitors for nearly 1,500 years. It is the one sight no first-time visitor should skip. Go early in the morning to beat the crowds, and dress modestly since it is an active mosque.

signature.name: Topkapi Palace
signature.detail: The opulent seat of the Ottoman sultans, with courtyards, harem rooms and treasury collections overlooking the water. Allow at least half a day to explore it properly. Buy tickets in advance and arrive at opening time to avoid queues.

signature.name: Blue Mosque
signature.detail: A working mosque famous for its cascading domes and blue Iznik tiles, standing right across from Hagia Sophia. Visit outside prayer times, cover shoulders and knees, and carry a scarf for women.

signature.name: Basilica Cistern
signature.detail: An eerie underground reservoir of hundreds of columns and dim reflected light, with the famous Medusa heads. It is a cool, quick stop on hot days. Tickets are timed, so book ahead and go early or late.

signature.name: Galata Tower
signature.detail: A medieval stone tower giving the classic panorama over the Golden Horn and old city rooftops. The viewing balcony is small, so go at opening or near sunset. It sits at the end of Istiklal Avenue, easily reached on foot.

signature.name: Grand Bazaar of Istanbul
signature.detail: One of the world's oldest covered markets, a maze of thousands of shops selling carpets, jewellery and spices. It is an experience as much as a shopping stop. Go on a weekday morning, and bargain politely.

signature.name: Dolmabahce Palace
signature.detail: A lavish 19th-century waterfront palace blending European and Ottoman styles, with a spectacular ceremonial hall. Entry is by guided timed tour, so reserve a slot. It is a short walk or tram ride from the Bosphorus waterfront.

signature.name: Suleymaniye Mosque
signature.detail: Mimar Sinan's masterpiece, perched on a hill with sweeping views over the Golden Horn. It is calmer than the Blue Mosque and free to enter. Visit outside prayer times and dress modestly.

signature.name: Maiden's Tower
signature.detail: A tiny tower on an islet in the Bosphorus, one of the city's most photographed symbols. Boats shuttle to it from the Asian shore. Go in the late afternoon for soft light and shorter queues.

signature.name: Rumeli Fortress
signature.detail: A massive 15th-century fortress on the Bosphorus built before the Ottoman conquest, with towers and walls to climb. The walkways are steep, so wear sturdy shoes. It is best reached by boat or bus along the European shore.

transport: Metro or tram about $0.60-1 a ride; taxis moderate
